particulars: All names, dates, places, ages, wound counts, sentence lengths, the 21-day limit and the specific governors were dropped.

items.record: The case is a criminal murder-and-rape prosecution ending in a death sentence: "The jurors returned with their verdict of death."
items.reading: A regulatory or administrative announcement about a fringe activist, publisher or business, built on a consent agreement or settlement.
items.loss: The reading misidentifies the domain, the stakes and the kind of institution involved.

items.record: The target was a man with an intellectual disability who deferred to authority: "Washington would politely defer to any authority figure with whom he came into contact."
items.reading: A dissident or unorthodox actor on the fringe of public life, bound to the institution by licensing, funding or supervision.
items.loss: This is the specific personal vulnerability that made him easy to steer into a false confession.

items.record: Police drew out confessions to several crimes after a separate arrest: "police claimed he had 'confessed' to a total of five different crimes."
items.loss: This is the sequence by which an unrelated arrest led to a broad, indiscriminate set of confessions.

items.record: The confession contradicted the known facts: "Washington did not know the race of his victim... that he had stabbed her two or three times when the victim showed thirty-eight stab wounds."
items.reading: The reading only suggests that the shaped account might still describe real misconduct.
items.loss: The record shows the confession was plainly factually false, not merely ambiguous.

items.record: The confession was rehearsed until it was acceptable, and police led him to the scene: "Only on the fourth attempt at a rehearsed confession did authorities accept... police, who in the end had to help him pick out Williams' apartment."
items.reading: The reading lists how the account was manufactured as unknown, possibly a plea bargain or boilerplate.
items.loss: This is the concrete mechanism by which the authorities built the confession through repeated coaching.

items.record: Forensic evidence that cleared him was altered: "an amended forensic report was prepared (without additional testing being conducted) that said testing for the rare protein was 'inconclusive.'"
items.loss: This is a second channel of institutional fabrication: tampering with the physical evidence, not only shaping his statement.

items.record: His defense was one-sided and failed him: "only the State's psychologist testified... the defense did not offer any counter argument to the jury concerning a sentence of death."
items.reading: The reading lists whether he had a lawyer as unknown.
items.loss: This shows that his legal representation failed at both trial and sentencing.

items.record: Rescue came through an informal network of prisoners and volunteers: "another death row inmate... alerted Marie Deans (a non-lawyer...) and a lawyer... the firm secured a stay of execution... nine days before he was scheduled to die."
items.reading: The reading says the target had no strong community and that a fringe audience amplified the dispute publicly.
items.loss: Relief came from a fellow prisoner and outside advocates acting just in time, not from public escalation.

items.record: Procedural rules blocked exoneration despite DNA evidence: "Because Washington was time barred by Virginia law... he was not exonerated. Instead... commuted Washington's sentence to life imprisonment."
items.reading: The reading says the target is constrained by the signed document and cannot walk it back.
items.loss: The real obstacle after he was proven innocent was a legal deadline, not his signature.

items.record: Correction came in stages over many years: commutation, then a limited pardon, then release to parole, and finally "an absolute pardon, which acknowledged that Washington was wrongfully convicted."
items.reading: The reading predicts an unresolved split public, with the official record persisting and being cited.
items.loss: This is the actual path of resolution: a gradual official reversal through executive clemency, ending in full acknowledgment of innocence.

items.record: The real perpetrator was identified: "Kenneth Tinsley... pleaded guilty to Rebecca Lynn Williams' rape and murder."
items.loss: This is the outcome that settled the underlying truth.

items.record: There was an actual victim of a violent crime: "a 19-year-old mother of three was raped and stabbed... She could only describe her attacker as a Black man acting alone."
items.loss: This covers the crime itself and the vague, race-based description that made him a fit for the suspect profile.

items.record: His own response after release was mild: "This was a whole lot better than I expected."
items.reading: The reading guesses at humiliation, defiance or a martyr narrative.
items.loss: This is the subject's actual, understated reaction to freedom.
